He was previously head coach of the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]] and [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]]. English played for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] before a three-year professional career. ==Early life== English was born on September 24, 1988, in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]]. His mother, Brenda Fowlkes, and his father, Kim English Sr. raised English along with his two sisters Bria and Jessica and brother Kalil.{{cite news|last=O'Neil|first=Dana|title=Kim English's transformation|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7322095 |access-date=February 12, 2013|work=ESPN.com|date=December 6, 2011}}{{cite web|title=Kim English Bio|url=http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/english_kim00.html|work=mutigers.com|access-date=March 16, 2012|archive-date=March 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309123333/http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/english_kim00.html|url-status=dead}} During his senior season at [[Randallstown High School]], English averaged 18.2 points and 7.4 rebounds and was named MVP while leading Randallstown to their third consecutive state championship. After high school, English attended [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Preparatory School]] in Fitchburg, Massachusetts. English averaged 17.3 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game in 2007–08 while again earning team MVP honors. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|34=no|collapse=no|year=2008}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kim English | position = SG | hometown = [[Baltimore, MD]] | highschool = [[Randallstown High School]] (MD) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | commitdate = September 30, 2007 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 3 }} |} ==College career== English committed to attend the [[University of Missouri]] on September 30, 2007.{{cite web|title=Kim English|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/missouri/basketball/recruiting/player-Kim-English-71420|work=Rivals.com|access-date=March 16, 2012}} As a freshman, English worked his way into the starting lineup, starting 13 out of 16 Big 12 games. In the second round of the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]], with Missouri tied 79–79 with [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], English came off the bench to replace an injured [[J. T. Tiller]] and hit two free throws to give Missouri an 81–79 lead en route to an 83–79 victory.{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2009 |title=English proves clutch; Marquette's James struggles in return |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=294000010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190210003707/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=294000010 |archive-date=February 10, 2019 |access-date=March 16, 2012 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} English averaged 14 points per game as a sophomore while earning [[USBWA]] All-District honors, being named to [[Dick Vitale]]'s All-Improved Team, and earning Third Team All-Big 12 honors, becoming just the third Mizzou underclassmen to earn All-Big 12 honors. As a junior English was unable to improve upon his sophomore year campaign, averaging just 10 points per game. As a senior, English averaged 14.5 points per game and made 45.9% of his three-pointers, earning Third Team All-Big 12 honors for the second time.{{cite web|title=2012 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205391642|work=Big12Sports.com|access-date=March 16, 2012}} Leading Mizzou to the [[2012 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]] championship, Mizzou's second Big 12 tournament championship in four years, English was named the Big 12 tournament Most Outstanding Player after averaging 23 points and shooting 78 percent from the field.{{cite web|title=MU's English leads Big 12 all-tournament team |url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/03/10/3482799/mus-english-leads-big-12-all-tournament.html |work=KansasCity.com |date=March 10, 2012 |access-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313121738/http://www.kansascity.com/2012/03/10/3482799/mus-english-leads-big-12-all-tournament.html |archive-date=March 13, 2012 }} With 107 victories in four years, English, with teammates [[Marcus Denmon]] and Steve Moore won more games than any senior class in Mizzou basketball history.{{cite web|last=Paylor |first=Terez |title=Missouri seniors prepare for final game in Columbia |url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/02/28/3458158/mu-seniors-prepare-for-final-home.html |work=KansasCity.com |date=February 28, 2012 |access-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120301075335/http://www.kansascity.com/2012/02/28/3458158/mu-seniors-prepare-for-final-home.html |archive-date=March 1, 2012 }} ==Professional career== ===2012–13 season=== English was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 44th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On July 9, 2012, he joined the Pistons for the 2012 NBA Summer League. On July 12, 2012, he signed with the Pistons.{{cite news|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Second Round Draft Selection Kim English|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-second-round-draft-selection-kim-english|access-date=July 12, 2012|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2012}} He was assigned to the [[D-League]]'s [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] on December 12, 2012,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-assign-khris-middleton-and-kim-english-fort-wayne-mad-ants|title=Detroit Pistons Assign Khris Middleton And Kim English To Fort Wayne Mad Ants|work=NBA.com|date=December 12, 2012|access-date=December 12, 2012}} and was recalled a week later.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-recall-khris-middleton-and-kim-english-fort-wayne-mad-ants|title=Detroit Pistons Recall Khris Middleton and Kim English from Fort Wayne Mad Ants|work=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2012|access-date=December 19, 2012}} ===2013–14 season=== On July 7, 2013, English joined the Pistons for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On July 11, 2013, he was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2013/07/11/pistons-waive-everyones-favorite-second-round-pick-kim-english/|title=Pistons waive everyone's web|url=http://www.ktul.com/story/29325332/tu-promotes-shea-seals-hires-kim-english|title=TU Promotes Shea Seals; Hires Kim English|first=John|last=Moss|work=KTUL.com|date=June 15, 2015 |access-date=March 8, 2017}} On August 11, 2017, English was hired by [[Tad Boyle]] as an assistant coach for [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], replacing [[Jean Prioleau]], who became the new head coach at [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.cubuffs.com/news/2017/8/11/kim-english-named-assistant-mens-basketball-coach.aspx|title=Kim English Named Assistant Men's Basketball Coach|first=Troy|last=Andre|publisher=[[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffs]]|date=August 11, 2017|access-date=August 15, 2017}} Two years later, on April 10, 2019, English was hired by [[Rick Barnes]] as an assistant for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. He replaced [[Rob Lanier]] on the staff, who was hired as the new head coach at [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State]].{{cite news |last1=Wilson |first1=Mike |title=Kim English joins Vols, Rick Barnes as assistant coach |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/04/10/tennessee-vols-basketball-kim-english-rick-barnes/3421095002/ |access-date=10 April 2019 |publisher=Knoxville News Sentinel |date=10 April 2019}} On March 23, 2021, English was hired as the head coach of [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]].{{cite press release|url=https://gomason.com/news/2021/3/23/mens-basketball-george-mason-names-kim-english-mens-basketball-head-coach.aspx|title=George Mason Names Kim English Men's Basketball Head Coach|publisher=[[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]]|date=March 23, 2021|access-date=March 23, 2021}} On March 23, 2023, English was named the head coach of the [[Providence Friars]].{{Cite web |date=2023-03-23 |title=Kim English Named Providence College Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://friars.com/news/2023/3/23/mens-basketball-kim-english-named-providence-college-mens-basketball-coach.aspx |access-date=2025-03-31 |website=Providence College Athletics |language=en}} In his first season at Providence, he led the Friars to a 21–14 mark overall and a 10–10 record in Big East play. [[Devin Carter]], who flourished in his first season under English, became the 44th Friar drafted all-time in the NBA when he was selected with the 13th pick in the 2024 Draft by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In April 2024, English signed a six-year contract extension with the Friars. However, less than two years later, on March 13, 2026, Providence announced that English had been [[dismissal (employment)|fired]] at the conclusion of a second consecutive losing season.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48195478/providence-fires-kim-english-loss-st-johns|title=Providence fires Kim English after three seasons|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 13, 2026|access-date=March 13, 2026}} In April 2026, he was hired as an assistant coach at [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] under new head coach [[Michael Malone]].{{cite news |last1=Backer |first1=Justin |title=UNC Adds Former Providence Head Coach to Malone’s Staff |url=https://www.si.com/college/unc/tar-heels-adds-former-providence-head-coach-malone-staff |access-date=18 April 2026 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=14 April 2026}} Later that month, he informed UNC
